title: Explain Like I'm 5 or Whatever I Choose: Evaluating the Potential for Interactive Complexity in Language Model Responses
abstract: arXiv:2606.06788v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Given the increased use of large language models (LLMs) for reading and seeking information and the varying needs and backgrounds of users, direct manipulation of text can be a valuable mechanism for end-user control. However, enabling direct manipulation requires that models generate text consistent with user-requested changes. We focus on one such setting, manipulating the complexity of scientific information, and ask if models can generate multiple summaries along a continuum of text complexity that enable effective user selection and control. Through a within-subjects user study, we identify reliable complexity measures and a criterion for how models should conform to these measures. We evaluate five LLMs of different families, sizes, and reasoning abilities on $557$ scientific queries. translated_abstract: 鉴于大型语言模型（LLMs）在阅读和获取信息方面的使用日益增多，以及用户需求和背景的多样性，对文本进行直接操纵可以成为终端用户控制的一种有价值机制。然而，实现直接操纵要求模型生成与用户所请求的更改相一致的文本。我们聚焦于其中一个场景——操纵科学信息的复杂度，并探讨模型能否沿着文本复杂度的连续区间生成多个摘要，从而实现有效的用户选择与控制。通过一项被试内用户研究，我们确定了可靠的复杂度度量指标以及模型应符合这些指标的准则。我们在557个科学查询上评估了五个来自不同家族、不同规模和不同推理能力的大型语言模型。我们发现，尽管模型能够在不同响应之间调整复杂度，但大多数变化仍然不一致，模型在调整复杂度指标时会……
tldr: 本研究通过用户研究确定了可靠的文本复杂度度量标准及模型遵循准则，并在557个科学查询上评估了五个大语言模型沿复杂度连续区间生成摘要的能力，发现模型虽能调整响应复杂度，但大多数变化仍与要求不一致。
en_tdlr: This study identifies reliable text complexity measures and conformance criteria through a within-subjects user study, and evaluates five LLMs on 557 scientific queries, finding that although models can vary response complexity, most changes remain inconsistent with user-requested levels.
